headline: Some Silicon Valley tech workers are turning to unions and worker groups over AI job fears and company politics, though a veteran local activist doubts AI alone will start a wave.
score_reason: Kept at the pool score: a well-sourced feature with figures, but built on organizers' accounts with no new union drive or decision.
importance_line: What changed is that AI anxiety is pushing some white-collar tech staff toward collective organizing, which affects software engineers and product staff first, then the companies they work for, but only a small share of tech workers are unionized and the report rests mostly on organizers' own accounts.
summary: KQED reports that, according to organizers, more Silicon Valley tech employees are turning to groups such as the Tech Workers Coalition, the Communications Workers of America and the Alphabet Workers Union, citing fears of AI-driven job loss, tracking of how much they use AI and their employers' government contracts. Only 3.7% of US computer and math workers are unionized against 10% across other industries, and one local activist and former Mountain View mayor quoted does not expect AI alone to push engineers to unionize unless the AI bubble pops.
notes: Full text read. Organizer quotes are their own views; figures attributed to the Bureau of Labor Statistics, Stanford and layoffs.fyi are as KQED gives them.
